1000254.etyen:
Internationalism, based ultimately on Portuguese Congo, from the name of the Kongo people and their kingdom, perhaps from Kongo nkongo (“hunter”). Another proposal connects the ethnonym with konga (“to gather”); its precise formation remains uncertain. The river was named after the people and kingdom, and the two modern states were in turn named after the river.
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Kongo, Danish Congo, Swedish Kongo, German Kongo, Dutch Congo and English Congo.

1004862.etyen:
From Antillene (“the Antilles”) + strøm (“current”), using the combining form Antiller- and the definite singular strømmen (“the current”), literally “the Antilles Current”.
The final element, strøm (“current”), ultimately continues Old Norse straumr (“stream, current”), from Proto-Germanic *straumaz (“stream, current”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *srew- (“to flow”). Cognates include Norwegian Nynorsk straum, Danish strøm, Swedish ström, Icelandic straumur, German Strom and English stream.
Parallel formations include Swedish Antillerströmmen, Dutch Antillenstroom, German Antillenstrom

1005118.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂éd
Compound of Fiss-dur (“F-sharp major”) + akkord (“chord”), literally “F-sharp-major chord”.
The first element Fiss-dur (“F-sharp major”) contains Fiss (“F-sharp”), the capitalized form of fiss, itself formed from f (“F”) and -iss (“sharp-note-forming suffix”); the suffix is from German -is (“sharp-note-forming suffix”), whose further origin is uncertain. The second part of Fiss-dur, dur (“major”), is via German Dur (“major”) from Middle High German bēdūre (“B-natural; hard B”), from Medieval Latin b durum (“hard B”). The adjective is from Latin dūrus (“hard”), from Proto-Italic
